Delegate walkout, protests greet Netanyahu as he addresses UN General Assembly. NEW YORK: Dozens of delegates walked out of the UN General Assembly hall on Thursday as hundreds of protesters gathered outside the building while Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu defended Tel Aviv’s actions amid growing international isolation, with elections looming that could threaten his political future. The walkout undersco­red the competing pressu­res facing Netanyahu, who is battling mounting criticism abroad over the Gaza conflict while campaigning for re-election at home ahead of an October 27 vote. On Thursday, Netanyahu delivered a combative address inside the General Assembly, where dozens of delegations walked out as he began speaking. The departing diplomats left large sections of the hall empty, creating a striking contrast with Netanyahu’s attempt to use the podium to present Israel’s case before the international community. Netanyahu responded by accusing his critics of hypocrisy and calling them “moral cowards.” He rejected allegations that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza, saying Israel had prevented rather than committed genocide. He defended the country’s military actions in Gaza and elsewhere in the region. Delegates walk out of the General Assembly hall as Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu arrives to address the 81st United Nations General Assembly at UN headquarters in New York City, US, September 24. — Reuters He also devoted a significant part of his speech to New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani, calling him “the antisemitic mayor of New York” and accusing him of spreading what Netanyahu described as lies about Israel. Mamdani, who had declined to join the street protests, responded after the speech. “Prime Minister Netanyahu used his speech to repeat baseless lies meant to sanitise his genocide of Palestinians,” Mamdani said. “No lie can change the fact that he remains the subject of an International Criminal Court arrest warrant alleging war crimes and crimes against humanity.” Mamdani previously said New York City lacked the authority to enforce the ICC warrant against Netanyahu, arguing that the appropriate authorities should carry it out. On Wednesday night, the mayor had hosted Palestinian families from Gaza at Gracie Mansion and planted an olive tree with them, saying: “May peace be our future.” The two scenes — protesters confronting his government’s policies on the streets and diplomats leaving the hall during his address — turned Netanyahu’s brief visit to New York into a day of parallel confrontation. Netanyahu’s stay had already been sharply shortened amid security concerns and expectations of protests. He arrived on Thursday morning, addressed the General Assembly and was scheduled to return to Israel the same evening rather than remain in New York overnight. Outside the UN, Jewish and Muslim activists, Palestinian supporters, human-rights campaigners, progressive Jewish groups, politicians, artists and musicians took part in separate demonstrations across Manhattan. Their messages varied, but opposition to Netanyahu’s government and Israel’s conduct of the Gaza conflict brought many of them into the streets at the same time. Demonstrators protest after Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s address to the United Nations 81st General Assembly in New York City, U.S., September 24. — Reuters The protests also offered a visible glimpse of a generational shift in American attitudes toward Israel and Netanyahu. While support for Israel remains stronger among older Americans, younger Americans have become substantially more critical of the Israeli government. A Pew Research Centre survey conducted in May found that only 18 per cent of Americans aged 18 to 29 had a favourable view of the Israeli government, compared with 47pc among those aged 65 and older. Among the youngest Americans, 58pc expressed a favourable view of Palestinians, compared with 47pc among those 65 and older. That generational divide was visible on the streets of New York, where many of the demonstrators were young people, including students, activists, artists and younger politicians. The largest direct action outside the UN was organised by Jewish Voice for Peace, whose New York chapter brought hundreds of protesters to First Avenue and 39th Street. Demonstrators wearing matching white T-shirts sat in the roadway, chanting against Netanyahu and calling for an end to US support for Israel. For a while, protesters stood and sat in the street, linking arms and blocking traffic as police moved in to clear the roadway. The chants continued as officers began making arrests. At least 30 people, including actors and politicians, were arrested in the initial action. Police later said more than 100 protesters had been taken into custody. Among those detained were actors Susan Sarandon and Hannah Einbinder, congressional candidate Darializa Avila Chevalier and City Council member Chi Ossé. Musicians Julien Baker and Lucy Dacus and actor Elliott Page were also among the prominent figures taking part in the protests. Chelsea Manning, who joined the protest, said people outside government institutions needed ways to reject policies they regarded as imperialism, ethnic cleansing and genocide. “We can’t be in there. This is the closest that we can get,” she said. Manijeh Moradian, a university professor of Iranian and Jewish heritage who participated in the demonstration, said protesters had a responsibility to speak out against what was happening in Gaza with US support. Jewish groups divided The demonstrations also highlighted divisions within New York’s Jewish community. Progressive Jewish organisations, including New York Jewish Agenda, T’ruah, J Street, New Jewish Narrative, New Israel Fund and Partners for Progressive Israel, held a separate protest at Dag Hammarskjöld Plaza near the UN. “We are gathered here as American Jews, Israelis, New Yorkers, to say: You are not welcome here,” said Margo Hughes-Robinson, executive director of New York Jewish Agenda. T’ruah, a rabbinic human-rights organisation, called for a ceasefire and accountability for alleged war crimes. The organisers described their rally as an alternative for Jewish New Yorkers who opposed Netanyahu’s policies while retaining concern for Israel and Jewish security. They were confronted by pro-Netanyahu counter-protesters who blew whistles, used megaphones, chanted “Bibi”, and sang Israel’s national anthem. On the other side, the ultra-Orthodox anti-Zionist group Neturei Karta also demonstrated, arguing that opposition to Israel could not automatically be equated with antisemitism. Elsewhere, Jewish and Muslim demonstrators marched together towards the UN, while Palestinian activists and other organisations joined the broader mobilisation against Netanyahu. A city divided over Israel and Gaza As police loaded detained protesters onto buses outside the UN, Netanyahu was speaking inside a building protected by heavy security. Outside, demonstrators sought to challenge the Israeli prime minister’s account of the Gaza conflict; inside, diplomats expressed their opposition by leaving the chamber. The contrast was difficult to miss. For several hours on Thursday, New York’s streets and the UN General Assembly hall became parallel stages for the same international argument — one expressed through demonstrations and arrests outside, the other through a diplomatic boycott inside. And beneath both scenes was a changing American debate over Israel.

'Tremendous things will be happening': Trump hails 'very productive' meeting with China's Xi. US President Donald Trump on Friday concluded his “productive” meeting with Chinese President XI Jinping, noting in a post on Truth Social that “tremendous things will be happening”. “Like almost everyone else, he seemed to like calling the poorly and inaccurately named artificial intelligence to a far more accurate and important name: super intelligence. That would be ‘super!’ Everyone last night agreed, also,” he wrote. The lavish state summit at the White House appeared heavy on symbolism but light on substance, with no sign of major breakthroughs between the world’s biggest economies. Still, Trump highlighted progress under a bilateral trade mechanism , citing what he described as increased market access for US farmers and ranchers, while both leaders identified artificial intelligence as an area for cooperation. Trump would follow up his summit with Xi by taking the Chinese leader to the US National Archives, where they were expected to stress views about the history and direction of ties between their countries. A newspaper featuring a front page photo of China’s President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump, at a White House welcome ceremony, is seen at a news stand in Beijing on September 25, 2026. —AFP Trump said in remarks welcoming Xi that they would see some of the greatest treasures of US history at the National Archives, including the Declaration of Independence, the US Constitution and the Bill of Rights. They would also see “artifacts testifying to the long and cherished relationship” between China and the United States and their “cultural exchanges”, he said. “Just as our ancestors reached across the ocean centuries ago to trade, to learn, and to build a better world, our two countries do really the same thing, and we’re very proud of it and the relationship,” Trump said. China has not commented on the visit to the archives, but analysts say Xi may be keen to see records relating to the US switch of recognition to communist China from Taiwan in 1979. China presses on Taiwan Xi has long sought to persuade Trump to state publicly that the United States opposes Taiwan’s independence , rather than saying only that it does not support independence, which has been Washington’s formulation for decades. He is also keen to get the US to halt arms sales to the island. As expected, Xi pressed Trump on Taiwan on Thursday, saying he hoped the United States would “handle the Taiwan question with prudence.” China’s state news agency also reported that Xi “hopes the US side will adhere to the correct position of opposing ‘Taiwan independence’.” While the United States, like most countries, has no formal diplomatic relations with Taipei, Washington is its most important international backer and is bound by US law to provide it with the means to defend itself. America’s Asian allies will watch closely to see how Trump talks about Taiwan following Xi’s visit. After his May summit with Xi, Trump, whose administration in December approved an $11 billion arms sale package to Taiwan, said he was holding a second package, worth some $14bn, in abeyance and described it as a “very good negotiating chip.” Craig Singleton of the Foundation for Defence of Democracies think tank said Beijing may believe it has established a new baseline on Taiwan with Trump. (L-R) China’s First Lady Peng Liyuan, China’s President Xi Jinping, US President Donald Trump and US First Lady Melania Trump look on during a military review in the Rose Garden of the White House in Washington, DC, on September 24, 2026. —AFP He said Xi’s use of the word “adhere” was revealing because “it implies Beijing believes Washington is already behaving in ways it wants.” “In the context of the current stand-down on Taiwan arms sales, China may increasingly view that restraint as a new baseline rather than a temporary pause,” he said. “Beijing’s objective is to get Trump to absorb Chinese red lines into his own definition of a stable relationship.” On Thursday, Senate Democrats criticised the summit, saying Trump had failed to secure meaningful concessions from Beijing on trade, security, artificial intelligence or human rights. They also criticised Trump for failing to publicly address China’s military pressure on Taiwan and called for the immediate delivery of approved military aid and arms sales to the island.

Lawyer challenges Islamabad-Peshawar Motorway closure in IHC. ISLAMABAD: A lawyer moved the Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Friday against the closure of the Islamabad-Peshawar Motorway (M-1) and sought directions to reopen the blocked routes for lawyers, litigants and emergency services. The government announced the motorway’s closure earlier this week as it stepped up arrangements to prevent the PTI from marching on Islamabad. The march was part of the party’s planned nationwide protest to demand the release of its jailed founder, Imran Khan, and mobilise people for the supremacy of the Constitution. The protest was originally planned for Sept 27, but the party has now reportedly deferred it. Advocate Mian Shafqat Jan, a lawyer of the Supreme Court, filed a petition on Friday against the government’s move to shutdown the M-1 Motorway after he was unable to reach the Peshawar High Court (PHC) to appear in a case due to the closure. According to the petition, the lawyer was scheduled to appear before the PHC on Sept 24. He managed to enter the motorway from the Islamabad toll plaza at around 7am after facing difficulties but found the route closed at the M-1 Attock Bridge. The petitioner said he sought information from officials deployed at the site about any written order authorising the closure but was unable to obtain a confirmation. He contended that closing public routes without a notification, written order or disclosed reasons infringed citizens’ fundamental rights and warranted judicial intervention. The petition named the federation through the interior and information secretaries, the inspectors general of the National Highways and Motorway Police and Islamabad Police, the National Highway Authority through its chairman, the Islamabad Capital Territory administration through the chief commissioner, and the Punjab government through its home secretary and inspector general of police as respondents. The petitioner also referred to a recent IHC judgement about the planned PTI protest, arguing that the court had recognised constitutional protections for citizens, including freedom of movement and access to courts. In its detailed 37-page judgement in the case pertaining to the PTI’s planned protest, the IHC held that any activity resulting in the infringement of citizens’ fundamental rights amounted to a violation of the Constitution. It also observed that the right to peaceful assembly could not be exercised in a manner that infringed the rights of other citizens. The bench, headed by Chief Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar and comprising Justice Muhammad Azam Khan and Justice Muhammad Asif, directed the authorities to ensure that no political party, leader or public office holder occupied roads, highways, interchanges or toll plazas in a manner that obstructed free movement or hindered access to medical and educational facilities. On the basis of these arguments, Advocate Jan urged the high court in his plea to declare the closure of roads and highways without any notification, written order or disclosed reasons illegal and unconstitutional. He has also sought directions for the interior secretary, communications secretary and Islamabad chief commissioner to ensure the reopening of blocked routes for emergency traffic, lawyers, litigants, witnesses, sick persons, funeral processions and other emergency services. According to the National Highways and Motorway Police (NHMP), the M-1 has been closed to all traffic in both directions between the Islamabad Toll Plaza and Chhachh Interchange, while the M-14 was closed from Hakla to Kundal. The GT Road was also closed at Attock Khurd. The government had also decided to close the Islamabad-Dera Ismail Khan Motorway (M14) — also known as the CPEC road — and GT Road. Security arrangements were also intensified in Attock, with containers and sandbags placed at key bridges and security tightened at major entry and exit points, as authorities prepared for the PTI protest. The federal government also approved the deployment of Rangers in Islamabad and several districts of Punjab ahead of the PTI’s planned march on the federal capital. Punjab has already imposed a ban on gatherings across the province for 13 days and prohibited inciting people to “unlawful assembly”. A similar ban under Section 144 has been enforced in Islamabad as well for two months. Gatherings in the federal capital are also banned under the Peaceful Assembly and Public Order Act 2024 , which had been rushed through the National Assembly amidst the opposition’s outcry ahead of a PTI gathering . Meanwhile, Section 144 has also been imposed in Karachi, Hyderabad, Sukkur and Balochistan. The Punjab government had also sent a letter to the federal interior ministry requesting mobile and internet services at specific locations in Rawalpindi and Attock to be downgraded or jammed on Sept 27 due to the “expected law and order situation”.

Indian police use tear gas against protesters seeking election chief's ouster. Indian police used tear gas and water cannons on Friday to disperse opposition Congress party members during nationwide protests demanding the resignation of the head of the election commission, whom they accuse of manipulating voter rolls. The “cockroach” youth movement, which counts millions of supporters and forced the education minister out in July, said it would launch protests across India on Oct 2 if Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar does not resign by Saturday. The protests, which are backed by other opposition groups, mark a new political challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi as Kumar, 62, a former civil servant, was appointed to head the independent Election Commission of India by Modi’s government. “Theft of votes is happening across the country,” local Congress party leader Amarinder Singh Raja said in Chandigarh in the northwest, one of at least two places where police fired water cannon after protesters climbed buses and barricades. Congress and other opposition parties have accused the eleciton commission of colluding with Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) to manipulate voter lists and win state elections in recent years, charges both the commission and the BJP have denied. Kumar himself has not commented. Newspaper reports dissent within the commission In at least a dozen of India’s 28 states, Congress supporters shouted slogans against Kumar, held up posters demanding his arrest and in one instance, burned an effigy of him and Modi. In the capital Delhi, hundreds of protesters climbed barricades and hurled insults at a man wearing a Kumar mask. The demonstrations were triggered by a report in the Indian Express newspaper on Wednesday that Kumar’s deputies had questioned him over changes to voter lists that opposition groups say benefit Modi’s BJP. “For three years, I have been exposing vote theft. Now, the election commissioners themselves are acknowledging it and bringing the truth to light,” Congress leader Rahul Gandhi said late on Thursday, referring to Kumar’s deputies. “Gyanesh Kumar has committed treason. He should resign immediately,” he added. The Election Commission said differences among officers were normal in any institution and that all its actions were lawful. The BJP dismissed the report and said that opposition parties were indulging in a smear campaign because popular support for the BJP meant they lost elections. State elections next year — including in the most populous state, Uttar Pradesh, and Modi’s home state of Gujarat, both ruled by the BJP — are key tests of support ahead of parliamentary elections due in 2029.

FBR sets up faceless tax audit, assessment centre in Islamabad. ISLAMABAD: The Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) has established the National Faceless Centre in Islamabad, under which audits and assessments will be handled by “faceless” wings to reduce official discretion and direct contact between tax officials and taxpayers. The initiative has been taken under Pakistan’s New Tax Operating Model and was approved by the government in principle in June. The centralised and faceless tax model is similar to systems used in the UK, Australia, the Netherlands, Singapore and India. It is designed to eliminate physical contact between tax authorities and taxpayers to prevent corruption. The decision to establish the National Faceless Centre was taken the Board in Council — a body headed by the FBR chairperson — in its meeting on Friday, an FBR statement said. It described NFC as a major reform that “changes how tax audits and assessments are carried out in Pakistan”. Until now, a taxpayer whose return was picked for audit had to deal with a particular officer in a particular office, often in person. Under the new system, that contact ends. Cases will be selected by a computerised, risk-based system rather than by any officer. Each case will then be assigned automatically to an officer who may be sitting anywhere in the country. The taxpayer will not know who the officer is, and the officer will have no say in which case comes to them. Every case will pass through three separate hands. One officer will conduct the audit, a second will make the assessment, and a third will review the work for quality before any order is issued. No single officer will control a taxpayer’s case from start to finish. All notices, replies and hearings will take place electronically through FBR’s IRIS system, and where the law requires a physical verification or recovery, it will be carried out by a separate field team, the statement detailed. The NFC draws its legal authority from the Finance Act, 2026. It will be headed by an Inland Revenue chief commissioner, with dedicated wings for faceless audit, faceless assessment, quality control and field operations. A Programme Management Unit has already been set up to oversee its rollout. “The purpose of the reform is same rules for every taxpayer, decisions based on data rather than personal judgement, and an end to the face to face contact that has long been a source of complaints. FBR expects the NFC to make tax proceedings faster, fairer and more transparent for taxpayers across Pakistan,” the statement said.

Info ministry dismisses Afghan claims of destroying Pakistani post near border in Balochistan as 'fake'. The information ministry dismissed on Friday claims by the Afghan defence ministry of a Pakistani post having been destroyed near the Spin Boldak border — the frontier between Balochistan and Kandahar — as “fake and fabricated”. The information ministry also took note of Afghan claims that there had been no casualties among the Afghan forces in the latest episode of clash between the two sides. “The claim is fake and fabricated. As per actual facts, an attempted Afghan aggression in the Gulistan sector was thwarted on night between Sept 24 and Sept 25, and during the process and subsequent heavy punishment inflicted on opposing Taliban posts, at least 13 Afghan Taliban personnel were killed and several injured,” the information ministry said in a post on X. It also shared visuals in the post, which the ministry said were of the incident. The incident, it added, had already been “widely covered by media and circulated extensively across social media, providing visual evidence of the border engagement and punishment inflicted on the Afghan Taliban after their cowardly attack”. “The […] Afghan ministry’s attempt is no surprise since the Taliban are habitual liars having no moral and reputational standing,” it added. The latest clash has taken place amid an uptick in tensions at the Pak-Afghan border. Pakistan conducted precision aerial and drone strikes in 10 locations across Afghanistan on Thursday in retaliation for drones launched from the neighbouring country a day earlier. The response came after eight drones, launched from Afghanistan, entered Pakistani airspace near the Torkham border and Kohat on Wednesday. Security sources said they were subsequently shot down. It was also reported that the Afghan Taliban engaged in unprovoked firing the night before near Kurram as security forces foiled an attempt by terrorists to cross into Pakistan. On Sept 21, Pakistan, in response to recent terrorist attacks in KP, conducted “calibrated” airstrikes in the border region with Afghanistan against terrorist hideouts and safe havens of terrorist organisations. A statement from the information ministry on Monday said that over 28 terrorists were eliminated in the strikes. “It is a matter of grave concern that Afghanistan continues to remain a hub of terrorism,” the ministry said at the time, specifying that the “threat to Pakistan emanates from Afghanistan”. The airstrikes had come after a major attack in the old Police Lines in KP’s Kohat claimed 23 lives and injured about 100 others. Eight terrorists were killed during an overnight clearance operation launched to clear the area. Ghazab lil-Haq Information Minister Attaullah Tarar described Monday’s action as part of Pakistan’s ongoing counter-terrorism campaign, Ghazab lil Haq. On the night of February 26, following unprovoked firing by the Afghan Taliban from across the border, Pakistan launched Operation Ghazab lil Haq against terrorist hideouts. Pakistan also carried out strikes in the border region with Afghanistan in late June , with the government saying they were in response to a wave of terrorist attacks, including one on a Rangers camp in Karachi . At the time, Tarar said that 25 terrorists were killed in those strikes in Paktia, Paktika and Kunar. Pakistan had carried out similar strikes on terrorist hideouts along its border with Afghanistan earlier that month, killing 26 terrorists. In July, security forces responded to unprovoked firing by the Afghan Taliban at border posts in Kurram, security sources had said. In the same month, the Afghan Taliban regime launched four rudimentary drones across the border into Balochistan, which were shot down by security forces. Two drones were also shot down in June in Qila Abdullah and Chagai districts. Pak-Afghan ties As clashes continue, tensions between Islamabad and Kabul have remained high. Islamabad has repeatedly urged the Taliban administration in Kabul to dismantle terrorist sanctuaries on Afghan soil, particularly those linked to the banned TTP, that are used for attacks in Pakistan. Officials say those appeals have gone unheeded. Earlier this week, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar addressed a meeting of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC), where he called for steps towards concrete and verifiable action to prevent the use of Afghan soil for terrorism against any neighbouring country, particularly Pakistan. Dar said Pakistan was “seriously concerned” about the presence of over two dozen terrorist groups in Afghanistan that threatened regional and international peace and security. Last week, Pakistan also told the UN Security Council that it would respond to terrorist threats emanating from Afghanistan in self-defence as and when needed and in accordance with international law. Earlier this month, the Foreign Office (FO) declared that meaningful progress in relations with Kabul would depend on the Taliban taking concrete and verifiable action against Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and other terrorist groups operating from Afghan territory. It maintained that while Islamabad welcomed China’s continuing engagement, the external facilitation could not substitute for action by Kabul against terrorist infrastructure. According to a UN Security Council-mandated monitoring report — covering the period from December 16, 2025 to June 9, 2026 — Afg­han Taliban’s continued support for TTP has contributed to a rise in the frequency and lethality of terrorist attacks in Pakistan, even as Kabul has taken some initial steps to rein in the group. The report also pointed to growing operational and facilitation linkages among the TTP, Al Qaeda, Islamic State-Khorasan (ISIL-K) and the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA).

33 India-sponsored terrorists killed by security forces in Balochistan since Sept 21: ISPR. Security forces have killed 33 terrorists in counter-terrorism operations in Balochistan since Sept 21, the military’s media affairs wing said in a statement on Friday. Terrorists from Fitna-al-Khawarij and Fitna-al-Hindustan were targeted in the operations, according to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR). The state uses the term Fitna al-Khawarij for the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and refers to designated Balochistan-based groups as Fitna al-Hindustan to highlight India’s role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan. Detailing the operations, the ISPR said that on Sept 24, as part of the ongoing Operation Shaban, security forces “busted additional terrorist hideouts, and after an intense fire exchange, five “India-sponsored terrorists” were killed. This took the tally of killed terrorist to 22, it added. “Weapons, ammunition and explosives were also recovered from khawarij locations. The clearance operation will continue till the complete neutralisation of threat from the area,” the statement said. In another engagement on Sept 25, security forces conducted an intelligence-based operation in the Nushki district. “During the conduct of [the] operation, own troops effectively engaged [the] terrorists’ hideout and after an intense fire exchange, 11 terrorists were sent to hell,” the ISPR stated. “[The] relentless counter-terrorism campaign under the vision ‘ Azm-i-Istehkam ’ (as approved by [the] Federal Apex Committee on National Action Plan) by security forces and law enforcement agencies of Pakistan will continue at full pace to wipe out [the] menace of foreign-sponsored and -supported terrorism from the country,” the military’s media wing added. President Asif Ali Zardari paid tribute to the security forces for the successful operations, according to a statement from the Presidency. “Eliminating 33 India-backed terrorists in Balochistan is a commendable achievement for the security forces,” he was quoted as saying, praising security personnel for seizing weapons and ammunition from the terrorists. “The nefarious designs of India-backed terrorist elements will be thwarted at all costs,” he vowed. Balochistan has witnessed an increase in terrorist attacks in recent weeks, prompting security forces to intensify counter-terrorism operations. The number of terrorist attacks in the province increased by seven per cent from 83 in July to 89 in August, according to a monthly assessment by the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies. On Wednesday, the ISPR said security for­ces had killed 19 terrorists in separate intelligence-ba­s­ed operations in Sha­ban, Kech and Quetta West during which a soldier was also martyred. On September 22, six terrorists were killed and nine suspected individuals were arrested during an intelligence-based operation by security forces in Balochistan’s Saran Tangi area, state-run Radio Pakistan reported . According to Radio Pakistan , a large cache of ammunition and weapons were also recovered from the possession of the terrorists. Earlier that day, security forces killed four more terrorists belonging to a banned organisation in an intelligence-based operation carried out in two areas of Panjgur district. According to officials, security forces launched an intelligence-based operation on the information about the presence of armed militants in Koh-Prom and the Aphan area of Panjgur district. “Four armed terrorists of Fitna al Hindustan were killed in the heavy gun battle during the operation,” they said, adding that a large quantity of arms and ammunition was seized from the hideouts of the terrorists.

PTI postpones Islamabad long march to Oct 4. ISLAMABAD/PESHAWAR: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi said on Friday that the PTI’s long march towards Islamabad, which was originally scheduled for Sept 27, would now commence from Peshawar on Oct 4. The announcement by the KP CM came during a press conference in Peshawar, where he said the PTI’s political committee had held a meeting and “unanimously agreed” to now commence the march on Oct 4 from Peshawar. “This struggle of ours is just for the supremacy of the Constitution, restoration of the independent judiciary, media freedom and Haqiqi Azadi , as envisioned by Imran Khan,” he added. The PTI has been gearing up for a nationwide protest and march towards Islamabad to press for the release of its founder, Imran Khan, who is currently incarcerated in Rawalpindi’s Adiala jail. Afridi claimed that Imran would be out of jail within half an hour if justice was served. But, he rued, court directives were not being abided by, referring to court orders for Imran’s medical treatment and meetings with his family. “So when you are not heard even after adopting all legal and constitutional means, the Constitution allows you to protest peacefully,” he added. Afridi further condemned the reported arrests and detentions of PTI leaders and workers, including ministers. He alleged that Punjab authorities had been directed to take action in KP and denounced the authorities for placing containers and hammering nails on roads along the KP-Punjab boundary to block the march’s route. Coming back to the postponing of the march, he remarked the PTI workers “know that it is a Test match”. He added that the PTI’s allies had also been informed of the party’s decision. Earlier in the day, amid speculation that the march would be postponed, Afridi sounded resolute that the march would take place. However, he did not specify at the time whether the protest would be delayed. The PTI would hold the Islamabad march whether they hammer nails into the roads, place containers, or fire bullets, he said while addressing a press conference in Peshawar. “The PTI will not step back from its demand for Imran Khan’s release and medical treatment despite threats of arrests and governor’s rule,” he added. Earlier, a senior PTI leader, who requested anonymity, had also told Dawn that the march would now leave from Peshawar on Oct 4. “There was a proposal to exhaust the federal government and law enforcement agencies, as they have already closed down the federal capital and a number of routes,” he said. The leader claimed that the PTI had already achieved what it wanted to do via the march. “They have closed down roads and are spending hundreds of millions on law enforcement,” he noted. Asked if the PTI intended to march alongside the Jamaat-i-Islami (JI), which had postponed its own protest march against the petroleum levy on the request of the premier, the leader said that the decision had nothing to do with them. “We are capable of arranging the march on our own,” he said. The development comes a day after a PTI leader had hinted at the possibility of postponing its protest march if the federal government agreed to hold elections within six to eight months, release Imran and other political prisoners, and investigate the May 9 and November 26 crackdowns on the opposition party. Advocate Naeem Haider Panjutha told Dawn that the protest could be postponed if these three assurances were given by the government. Party spokesperson Sheikh Waqas Akram, however, had denied any such proposal was being discussed at any party forum, saying only Imran could take a decision even if such a proposal was on the table. Meanwhile, preparations in the Rawalpindi Division and the federal capital territory to maintain security and deal with any emergency situation have been in full swing in light of the potential long march and other protests in Islamabad. Punjab has already imposed a ban on gatherings across the province for 13 days and prohibited inciting people to “unlawful assembly”. A similar ban under Section 144 has been enforced in Islamabad for two months. The Punjab government has also sent a letter to the interior ministry requesting mobile and internet services at specific locations in Rawalpindi and Attock to be downgraded or jammed on Sept 27. Meanwhile, the federal government on Thursday approved the deployment of Rangers in Islamabad and several districts of Punjab from Sept 20 to Oct 5. “The deployed troops may respond appropriately in self-defence to any threats or violent activities encountered in the course of their duties as per rules/regulations in vogue,” the notification stated. HRCP urges govt to de-escalate political tensions All three of Imran’s sisters — Uzma Khan, Noreen Khan and Aleema Khan — have been detained and there have also been reports of the arrests of PTI members and workers. The Human Right Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) said in a statement on Friday that it “deplores the mounting arrests and preventive detention of PTI workers, lawmakers and leaders ahead of the party’s planned protest march”. Reports indicated that scores of workers, including women, had been arbitrarily detained, with some families claiming that they had no information as to the whereabouts of their relatives, the HRCP said. It added that it was “incumbent on the state to uphold the right to peaceful assembly for all citizens”. “Pre-emptive mass detention and restrictions on freedom of movement cannot be justified as proportionate or necessary. Moreover, repeated blanket restrictions, including the imposition of Section 144, are an affront to democratic principles. “We urge the government to de-escalate political tensions by resuming a purposeful dialogue with the opposition and to immediately release those who have been arbitrarily detained,” the HRCP said. Tarar takes aim at KP govt for ‘facilitating terrorism’ As political tensions persist between the PTI and the federal government, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar continued his criticism of the party and the KP government on Friday. Addressing a press conference in Islamabad, he accused the KP government of avoiding to take steps to maintain law and order in the province. He alleged that they also gave “full facilitation” to terrorists and called their policy on law and order “evasive”. “In one way or another, terrorists have attacked all political parties in KP,” the minister said. “But the PTI is held in high regard by terrorists. And not only do they avoid condemning terrorists, but they also fully avoid taking any sort of action against them. Facilitating terrorists is part of their policy.” He called KP’s PTI government the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan’s (TTP) “B-team”, and Tehreek-i-Taliban Afghanistan’s (TTA) “C-team”, claiming that it was facilitating the TTP while also “representing” the TTA. He also took aim at KP CM Afridi specifically, saying he “looks less like a chief minister and more like a TTP commander, in both his words and actions”. “When drones are fired at Kohat from Afghanistan, and the Pakistan Army and Air Force very skilfully take them down, you will not see any sort of condemnation or statement from KP government,” Tarar claimed. “When there is firing from Afghanistan in Kurram … you will never see them go to Kurram and say ‘We have come here, we stand with our forces, and we will not tolerate such firing under any circumstances’.” He termed this a sign of cowardice from CM Afridi, his cabinet and his entire KP government, adding that this was also the reason they were “running away” from protests. “They are not even prepared. I’ve just come from KP. They don’t have any sort of preparations,” the minister said. “Come and protest, if you have the courage,” he said. He stressed that the provincial government was in charge of controlling law and order, highlighting that 2,456 terror attacks had taken place in KP in 2026 — around 10 a day on average. He added that 472 police, army, rangers, and FC personnel were martyred and over 1,500 people injured this year. The information minister asserted that the reason the KP government did not want to fix the law and order situation was to maintain a “political terror-crime nexus” and illegal trade and mining activities in the province, through which they “funded terrorists”. “A provincial government which doesn’t want to stop terrorism and fix law and order, and countless citizens lose their lives — this cannot be justified in any part of the world,” he said.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs391.30 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs408.53 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable from Sept 26 (Saturday) to Sept 28 (Monday). Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm and fuel allocations for official vehicles has been cut by 50 per cent for three months. On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices. Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

Rs16bn bank-funded remittance reward scheme unveiled. • Rs4bn to be distributed among 2,521 winners in each quarterly draw • Each raffle to award Rs100m top prize; twenty Rs25m, 100 Rs10m and 2,400 Rs1m prizes • Beneficiaries receiving at least $100 in each of three months qualify automatically • First draw on Jan 15 next year for remittances received from Oct 1 to Dec 31 • Cash-over-counter, RDA remittances excluded from scheme KARACHI: State Bank Governor Jameel Ahmad on Friday launched the Pasban Remittance Reward Scheme, under which the banking industry will offer Rs16 billion in annual cash prizes to recipients of home remittances sent through formal channels, with no cost to the national exchequer. The scheme, launched under the auspices of the Pakistan Banks Association (PBA) and developed under the patronage of the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP), is aimed at encouraging overseas Pakistanis to send money through formal banking channels. It will distribute Rs4bn in prizes every quarter to 2,521 winners, or more than 10,000 winners annually. Each quarterly draw will offer one top prize of Rs100 million, 20 prizes of Rs25m each, 100 prizes of Rs10m and 2,400 prizes of Rs1m. The scheme rewards the person receiving the remittance in Pakistan instead of the sender abroad. Partici­pation is automatic and free, with no application, registration, ticket purchase or minimum-balance requirement. To qualify, a beneficiary must receive home remittances equivalent to at least $100 into an eligible bank account or wallet in each of the three months of a quarter. The number of entries increases with the value of each qualifying remittance. For example, a $260 remittance earns three entries, while $1,000 earns 10. There is no upper limit on the number of entries that an eligible account can earn. However, cash collected over the counter will not qualify, as the remittance must be credited directly to an eligible account or wallet. Roshan Digital Account inflows and remittances credited to foreign-currency accounts are also excluded. The first qualifying period will run from Oct 1 to Dec 31, 2026, and the first draw is scheduled for Jan 15, 2027. Prizes other than the top award will be distributed through regional pools, with 50 per cent allocated to remittances originating from the Gulf Cooperation Council countries, 15pc each to the United Kingdom and Europe, and 10pc each to North America and other countries. The Rs100m first prize will be open to eligible beneficiaries regardless of the country from which the remittance was sent. Speaking at the launch ceremony, the SBP governor said workers’ remittances were the backbone of millions of families, helping meet household expenses and supporting education, healthcare and investment. Mr Ahmad said Pakistan’s external account position had improved substantially and SBP’s foreign exchange rese­rves have jumped to $21.4bn from below $3bn in February 2023. He said the strengthening of foreign exchange buffers had been driven primarily by purchases from the market rather than accumulation of external debt. Meanwhile, workers’ remittances reached a record $41.6bn in FY26 compared to $21.7bn in FY19, nearly doubling over the period. Mr Ahmad said the government and SBP had over the years introduced various Home Remittance Incentive Schemes to encourage the use of formal channels. As those programmes expanded and their cost increased, the authorities began moving towards “a more sustainable, market-oriented model” funded in coordination with the banking industry. He said Pasban represented another step in that transition and would help maintain the attractiveness of formal remittance channels while recognising the contribution of overseas Pakistanis. The scheme’s terms and conditions state that Pasban builds on systems previously used for the Sohni Dharti Remittance Programme, which has been discontinued. Pasban is a separate scheme and points or rewards accumulated under Sohni Dharti will not be transferred to it. PBA Chief Executive and Secretary General Muneer Kamal said Pasban built on a remitter incentive funded by banks since July 2026, taking the banking industry’s annual commitment towards remittance-related support to close to Rs100bn. The draw process will be operated by 1LINK through an algorithm-based random selection system without manual intervention, while the entry-generation and draw systems will be independently audited. Prize money will be placed in escrow at the National Bank of Pakistan before each draw. Winners will be contacted by their banks and results will also be announced publicly without disclosing personal details. After verification, prizes will be credited in rupees to the winning accounts and applicable withholding tax will be deducted at source. Published in Dawn, September 26th, 2026

What Netanyahu’s ‘welcome’ tells us about young America. POLICE detain US actress Susan Sarandon and other pro-Palestinian demonstrators near UN headquarters in New York, ahead of the Israeli prime minister’s address to the UN General Assembly.—AFP WASHINGTON: The most striking feature of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s appearance in New York this week was not simply the hundreds of protesters outside the United Nations, or the diplomats who walked out when he began speaking; it was the people standing outside. They included Palestini­ans and other Muslims, but also Jews, Christians, secular Americans, professors, artists and young activists, who all said they could no longer remain silent about the destruction in Gaza. Something fundamental appears to be changing in America. Younger Americans increasingly view Israel and the Palestinians differently from their parents and grandparents. A Pew Research Center survey conducted in May found that only 18pc of Americans aged 18 to 29 had a favourable view of the Israeli government, compared with 47pc among those aged 65 and older. By contrast, 58pc of the youngest Americans had a favourable view of Palestinians, compared with 47pc among those 65 and older. Devastating images from Gaza are reshaping young people’s views of Israel However, only 13pc of young adults view Hamas favourably. That distinction is important because the polling shows that many younger Americans increasingly distinguish between Palestinians and Hamas, while becoming more critical of the Israeli government. Shibley Telhami, a University of Maryland political scientist, notes that the images confronting younger Americans are vastly different from those that shaped earlier generations. Older Americans came of age with memories of Israel’s creation after Holocaust and its early wars. Younger Americans have grown up watching Gaza on their phones — dead children, displaced families and destroyed neighbourhoods. For many, Gaza has become a formative political experience. The shift is also visible among American Jews. Pew found in 2026 that 83pc of Jewish Americans viewed the Israeli people favourably, while 47pc expr­essed a favourable view of the Israeli government. The relationship between Israel, its government and American Jewish identity is being debated more openly. That debate was visible on the streets of New York. Manijeh Moradian, a professor of Iranian and Jewish heritage, told reporters the destruction of Gaza was being carried out “in our name, with our tax dollars” and that people had a responsibility to speak out. Jewish organisations also held demonstrations near the UN. Groups including T’ruah, J Street, the New Israel Fund, the New York Jewish Agenda and Partners for Progressive Israel criticised Netanyahu’s government. At another protest organised by Jewish Voice for Peace, police arrested more than 100 people. Some protesters identify with liberal Zionism; others reject Zionism entirely. But they share opposition to Netanyahu’s government and the conflict in Gaza. Inside the UN, dozens of delegations walked out as Netanyahu began speaking. The prime minister defended Israel’s military campaign, rejected allegations of genocide and accused his critics of hypocrisy. He also turned his attention to New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani, whom he accused of antisemitism and spreading falsehoods. Mamdani responded after the speech, accusing Netanyahu of repeating “baseless lies meant to sanitise his genocide of Palestinians”. He added that Netanyahu remained the subject of an International Criminal Court arrest warrant alleging war crimes and crimes against humanity. Shortly before Netanyahu’s speech, Mamdani planted an olive tree at Gracie Mansion with Palestinian families from Gaza. “May peace be our future,” he wrote alongside a video of the ceremony. The gesture, occurring as Netanyahu addressed the UN and attacked him by name, offered a starkly different image of how the Gaza tragedy was being remembered in New York. The exchange illustrated a larger change. Israel’s relationship with America is no longer debated only in terms of its security or right to exist. Increasingly, especially among younger Americans, the question is what Israel is doing now. While the generational divide is not absolute and attitudes remain sharply divided by party and ideology, the age gap is clear. For a generation growing up with Gaza on its screens, Israel is being judged not primarily by the history that shaped their parents’ views, but by the images and events shaping their own lives. PM invites Achakzai for ‘direct talks’. ISLAMABAD: Soon after the opposition annou­nced its decision to extend the date of its long march, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday invited Leader of the Opposition in the National Assembly Mehmood Achakzai for direct talks, apparently in a bid to ensure political stability in the country. According to a source close to the prime minister, PM Shehbaz extended the invitation for dialogue, but no response had so far been received from the opposition leader. “Yes [the PM has invited Mr Achakzai], but nothing yet [from the opposition side],” the source said. A Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI) spokesman conf­irmed that the opposition leader had received the prime minister’s invitation. Before the latest invitation, the prime minister had already invited Mr Achakzai on Sept 11 for mandatory consultation on the appointment of a new chief election commi­ssioner (CEC). Prime Minister Sheh­baz, who is currently in the United States to attend the UN General Assembly, is expected to return within a few days. Before the prime minister’s first invitation to Mr Achakzai over the appointment of the CEC, National Assembly Speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq had urged both the prime minister and the opposition leader to sit together for consultations on the appointment of a new CEC. Under Article 213(2A) of the Constitution, the prime minister is required to consult the opposition leader in the National Assembly and forward three names for the appointment of the chief election commissioner to a parliamentary committee, which hears the candidates and confirms one of them. 6 million citizens registered under PM’s fuel relief scheme: Shaza Fatima. • Minister says over 6.18m tokens generated, 4.79m redeemed since launch • 24/7 control room monitoring implementation for ensuring transparency and timely resolution of issues ISLAMABAD: Federal Infor­mation Technology and Teleco­mmunication Minister Shaza Fatima Khawaja said on Friday that around 5.91 million citizens had been registered under the Prime Minister’s Fuel Relief Scheme since its launch. Addressing a news conference along with Minister of State for Finance and Railways Bilal Azhar Kayani, she said over 6.18 million fuel relief tokens had been generated, of which 4.79m had been successfully redeemed. Reiterating that the government had removed the five-litre limit for motorcycles, rickshaws and Qingqi following public feedback, she said the ownership requirement had also been remo­ved for motorcycle and rickshaw users who used rented vehicles. She said that amid volatility in global oil markets resulting from regional tensions in the Middle East, the fuel relief scheme was aimed at providing direct and targeted relief to citizens most affected by rising fuel costs. She reiterated that the scheme provided fuel relief to eligible two- and three-wheelers, including motorcycles, Qingqi and rickshaws, as well as cars up to 800cc. The scheme had been designed to ensure that relief reached eligible citizens through a simple, transparent and technology-enabled mechanism. The IT minister also displayed a live dashboard showing the total number of registrations, tokens generated and redeemed, as well as the provincial breakdown of the figures. Token figures The province- and region-wise breakdown of redeemed tokens included 210,032 in Islamabad Capital Territory, 3.07m in Punjab, 1.21m in Sindh, 267,460 in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, 6,761 in Balo­chi­stan, 23,796 in Azad Jammu and Kashmir and 4,845 in Gilgit-Baltistan. The minister underscored that the figures reflected the broad outreach of the scheme, with eligible citizens across all provinces and regions availing themselves of fuel relief. She said a 24/7 control room at the IT and Telecommunication Ministry was monitoring implementation of the scheme across the country. The control room was overseeing the process from registration and token generation to redemption, with a focus on ensuring transparency and timely resolution of issues. She said citizens facing any difficulty or requiring assistance regarding the scheme could call 9771 or visit the official website pmfuelrelief.pk for information and support. Ms Fatima said provincial governments and their administrations were playing an important role in overseeing the programme. She said around three meetings were being held daily to monitor its implementation, while officials were also present on the ground. She said she had personally visited petrol stations where people were facing problems and observed the implementation of the scheme. Awareness campaigns The minister thanked petrol pump dealers, oil marketing companies and the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) for facilitating citizens under the scheme and urged petrol pump staff to assist eligible people with registration and provide information about the facility. She said the government was conducting awareness campaigns and would also use the media to reach more people, particularly those affected by higher petrol prices. The minister said the government was also monitoring petrol stations through a live GIS map to identify facilities being used and address problems. Regarding older motorcycles, Ms Fatima said she had seen very few cases involving motorcycles registered before 2006. She added that there were some old cars, including Suzuki FX models, but said most of the people targeted by the subsidy were receiving the facility. She said the scheme was continuing smoothly and petrol pumps were being paid within a 24-hour cycle. With input from APP Published in Dawn, September 26th, 2026

Hybrid vehicle prices slashed. KARACHI: After a delay of nearly two weeks, assemblers have begun lowering prices for hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs) following the reduction in the general sales tax (GST) on vehicles up to 2,000cc, from 25 per cent to 18pc, effective Sept 13. Also on Friday, Mega Motor Company (MMC), BYD’s official partner in Pakistan, announced that “BYD has reached a major milestone of 10,000 vehicles on Pakistani roads, marking the fastest ramp-up by a new-entrant New Energy Vehicle (NEV) brand in the country’s automotive history”. Honda Atlas Cars Ltd (HACL) has revised the prices of HR-V e: HEV and HR-V VTIS to Rs9.299 million and Rs7.299m from Rs10.369m and Rs7.799m, respectively. HACL said the new prices are for a limited time and would be offered on limited stock. New retail prices will be applicable on all orders invoiced on and after Sept 25. Assemblers pass on GST cut after two-week delay According to a circular issued by the Indus Motor Company (IMC), the new prices of Toyota Corolla Cross HEV X and Cross HEV are Rs9.729m and Rs9.299m, respectively, down by Rs570,000 and Rs550,000. Chery Master Director Sales and Marketing Syed Asif Ahmed told Dawn that the government’s decision to settle the general sales tax (GST) issue at 18pc from 25pc on electrified vehicles may revive sales, as consumers had delayed their purchases, waiting for the government’s decision. Under the Automotive Industrial Development Policy (AIDP) 2021-26, which expired on June 30, the GST was 8.5pc on EVs. After the expiry of AIDP, the industry has been waiting for the new policy, which was expected to take effect from July 1, but it has yet to be announced. Assemblers believe that the absence of a clear policy framework had created uncertainty across the automotive value chain, affecting business planning, production scheduling and investment decisions. During the July-August period, several assemblers temporarily deferred vehicle invoicing due to the absence of clarity on the applicable policy and tariff regime. Mr Asif recalled that the 25pc GST caused a sharp drop in demand, leaving a sizable stock of assemblers’ electrified vehicles unsold until mid-September as consumers waited for clarity on the GST issue. “I think sales will return to normal in the coming months,” he said, adding that it is unclear whether GST will drop further or remain unchanged, depending on decisions in the new auto policy. On deliveries and bookings, he said most vehicles from his company and other assemblers will be delivered in the next two months. It also seems that completely knocked-down (CKD) kits are readily available at assemblers’ plants, despite geopolitical tension in the Middle East, as the Iran-US war has plunged the region into turmoil since Feb 28. Balochistan farmers postpone march on Islamabad. • Decision follows provincial govt assurances to address growers’ demands • Kissan Ittehad president calls on CM Bugti to declare agricultural emergency QUETTA: The Pakistan Kissan Ittehad has postponed its long march and sit-in towards Islamabad, which was scheduled to begin from Quetta on Friday, following a request and assurances from the Balochistan government. According to Home Affairs Adviser Babar Yousafzai, a government delegation led by Provincial Minister Ali Madad Jattak met Kissan Ittehad President Khalid Baath. Member of the Balochistan Assembly Mir Jahanzeb Mengal also attended the meeting. During the meeting, the government delegation assured the farmers’ leader that steps would be taken to address the demands of the farming community and fulfil their legitimate concerns. Mr Yousafzai said Khalid Baath acc­e­p­ted the government’s assurances and req­uest and announced the postponement of the long march towards Islamabad. He also assured the government delegation of the farmers’ cooperation. The home affairs adviser said the dialogue between the Balochistan government and the Kissan Ittehad was an important step towards progress. He added that the provincial government was taking serious measures to address the demands of the farming community. He said the protest would continue until their demands were accepted. Mr Baath said farmers’ caravans from across the country would join the Islamabad march. He said the movement aimed to highlight the agricultural problems faced by farmers and address the deteriorating condition in the agriculture sector.
